Key Takeaways

  • NRIs can repatriate proceeds from an Indian property sale, subject to RBI rules and limits (commonly up to USD 1 million per financial year).
  • The process needs correct tax handling, Form 15CA/15CB, and specific bank documentation.
  • Funds usually route through NRO to NRE/overseas accounts with proper certification.
  • Getting the documentation and TDS/tax right is what makes the transfer go through.
  • We guide the end-to-end process and coordinate the paperwork.

For NRIs, selling a Hyderabad property is straightforward compared to the next step: moving the money abroad. Repatriation is governed by RBI rules and requires precise tax and bank documentation.

JaaGa guides the repatriation — the tax certification (Form 15CA/15CB), the bank paperwork, and the RBI-compliant route — so your sale proceeds reach your overseas account cleanly.

When This Helps

After (or while) selling an Indian property as an NRI and needing to transfer the proceeds abroad.

When you're unsure about the limits, tax forms (15CA/15CB), TDS, or the NRO-to-NRE/overseas route.

  1. 1

Documents Required

  • Registered sale deed of the property

TDS on NRI sales

15CA/15CB errors

Why Property Repatriation (NRI) Matters

Many NRIs complete a sale and then get stuck for months at the bank because the tax certification or source-of-funds trail isn't right. Handling repatriation properly is what actually gets your money out of India, on time and within the rules.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much can an NRI repatriate?

Commonly up to USD 1 million per financial year from NRO funds, subject to RBI rules and proper documentation. Your specific case should be confirmed with your bank/CA.

What are Form 15CA and 15CB?

15CB is a chartered accountant's certificate on the remittance and its tax; 15CA is the declaration filed with the tax department. Both are typically needed to remit.

Is TDS deducted on my sale?

Yes — NRI property sales attract TDS, often at higher rates. Correct handling (and any refund) is part of the process.

Do you provide tax or legal advice?

We guide and coordinate the process and paperwork with your CA and bank; we are a facilitation service, not a substitute for personalised tax or legal advice.

Can this be done remotely?

Yes — the documentation and coordination are handled remotely for NRIs.
